Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the European Union (effective July 1, 2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Report and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, March 28, 2001, as amended), Enforcement Decree of the same Act (Presidential Decree No. 17286, as amended); Specialized Credit Finance Business Act (Act No. 5374, January 13, 1997, as amended); Act on the Regulation of Credit Business and Protection of Financial Users (Act No. 13737, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, January 27, 1962, as amended) Articles 19 and 289; Financial Supervisory Commission and Financial Supervisory Service rules requiring customer due diligence and beneficial owner verification; Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) guidance on identification and ongoing monitoring.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate) of each corporate shareholder / ultimate beneficial owner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction; for Korean entities, the Supreme Court Registry Office (Internet Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize by a local notary in the issuing country. If the issuing country is a Hague Apostille Convention state, obtain an Apostille from the competent national authority (Korea: Ministry of Foreign Affairs; USA: Secretary of State; UK: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office). If the issuing country is not a Hague state, obtain consular legalization from the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea in such country, followed by confirmation by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel, mutually exclusive routes and must not be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Recent Certificate of Corporate Existence / Business Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or tax authority in the jurisdiction of incorporation (Korea: District Tax Office; USA: Secretary of State; Hong Kong: Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize and then apply for Apostille (Hague member states) or consular legalization (non-Hague states) as per the parallel route described above; never combine both authentication methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of each corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa and appointing representatives / attorneys-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the respective shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sign the resolution before a local notary; then obtain an Apostille (Hague state) or consular legalization (non-Hague state) by the Republic of Korea diplomatic mission, using the same mutually exclusive parallel doctrine.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum / Statutes) of the ultimate corporate shareholder, duly notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or certified public notary in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticate the articles by notarization; thereafter proceed with either Apostille (Hague member) or consular legalization (non-Hague member) as separate parallel tracks in accordance with the Hague Apostille Convention or consular law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter covering the corporate shareholder's account standing and AML/KYC compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank where the shareholder maintains its primary operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The issuing bank officer's signature is notarized; afterwards the instrument is apostilled (Hague states) or consular legalized (non-Hague states) in the same mutually exclusive manner. The reference letter must be issued within 30 days of account review.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every individual shareholder holding twenty-five percent or more, and every natural person exercising effective executive control through a corporate chain, must undergo enhanced CDD under KoFIU and FSC regulations. The protocol mandates near-real-time screening against: (i) the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's internal PEP database and the official designation lists; (ii) OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, with the consolidated 50% ownership rule applied; (iii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list covering the DPRK and Iran; (iv) EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions; and (v) the domestic Korean list published under the Financial Transactions Report Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Automated fuzzy-matching is performed on all transliterated names, dates of birth, and passport numbers, with a system re-scan every 48 hours. Negative-media and litigation checks are run on the ultimate beneficial owners; PEP relationships are escalated to the compliance officer and, where required, the Financial Supervisory Service for approval before the filing of the Korean incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (I-REG) of the Supreme Court of Korea (interior registry portal: 인터넷등기소) for trade-name reservation and clearance, integrated with the National Tax Service's Homtax portal for subsequent business registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal trade name (sangho, 상호) must be expressed in Hangul; an auxiliary English trade name may be registered on a parallel basis if the Korean name remains the legal identifier. The name must contain the suffix 주식회사 (Chusik Hoesa). The standard four-tier naming convention is: (1) a geographical or brand descriptor (e.g., 'ASIA' or 'GLOBAL'), (2) the trade or activity description (e.g., 'TRADE', 'FACTOR', 'SUPPLYCHAIN'), (3) the industry-specific term (e.g., 'FINANCE' or 'FINANCING' - requiring prior FSC authorization for financial words), and (4) the statutory suffix 'Chusik Hoesa'. English words are transliterated phonetically using the Revised Romanization of Korea for the registry, but the hangul spelling controls.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On name rejection, the applicant or its counsel must file a written objection (이의신청) with the head of the local district registration court within one month of service of the rejection notice, setting out the legal grounds on which the requested name is distinguishable and not deceptive. The court holds a summary hearing and issues a decision within fourteen days. If the objection is denied, the applicant may file a formal appeal (항고) under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act to the appellate division of the district court within two weeks of the denial. Where the rejection originates from the National Tax Service at the business-registration stage, the applicant may request examination under Article 55 of the Framework Act on Tax Administration, then apply to the Tax Tribunal within ninety days, and ultimately institute administrative litigation before the Seoul Administrative Court. Extension of a valid name reservation is obtained by re-filing the same application before expiry, granting another one hundred eighty days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an active trade-finance and factoring company, virtual offices and commercial mailbox services are rejected by the Financial Supervisory Service and the National Tax Service as insufficient corporate substance. The Specialized Credit Finance Business Act and the Commercial Act require a fixed, physical registered office in Korea with dedicated signage, rented space, operational facilities (telephone, fax, server, files) and at least one full-time employee or registered officer present during business hours. A virtual office may be tolerated for a passive holding vehicle, but for ISIC 6492 (factoring, reverse factoring, trade-finance operations) the authorities will treat an internet-only address as an absence of substance, provoking license denial, bank account de-risking, or an administrative order to restore a physical office within thirty days.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection includes: (1) original lease agreement and utility bills in the entity's name; (2) payroll records and employment contracts for staff; (3) a visible company nameplate; (4) working IT infrastructure connected to the enterprise email domain; (5) corporate minutes and accounting ledgers; (6) an executive or statutory officer present at the registered address; (7) bank statements evidencing transactional correspondence with the registered postcode. Quantified risk: 85% likelihood of an unannounced inspection by the National Tax Service or Municipal Registry Officer within the first 12 months for a licensed factoring entity; for a non-licensed holding vehicle the risk drops to 15%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee under the Court Fees Act (tariff for name search and reservation)
Notary Fee Act (Korea) standard minimum for corporate notarization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration and Stamp Duty Act; 0.4% of paid-in capital with a minimum tariff basis of KRW 90,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of five foreign shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities in each jurisdiction (e.g., Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, U.S. Secretary of State, UK FCDO, Korean consulates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Public price lists: Korean MOFA apostille fee ~KRW 800 per item; foreign notary/secretary-of-state fees at market rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean translation of all foreign bundle documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of KRW 70,000 - 150,000 per A4 page for certified translations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO verification and enhanced PEP/sanctions screening (OFAC, UN, EU, KOFIU)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML compliance provider (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones, Refinitiv)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard bank administrative / notarial fee for reference letters, USD 50 - 150

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Articles 288 through 335 and Article 393, supplemented by the Notary Public Act for certification of the Articles of Incorporation, and the Credit Specialized Financial Business Act for the subsequent factoring license
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, acting through the Supreme Court Registration Information System (IROS) online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation under Article 317 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for formation of a Chusik Hoesa. However, all subscription proceeds must be deposited into a blocked capital-deposit account held at a licensed commercial bank or securities company in the Republic of Korea before the registration application is filed; the funds remain frozen and may not be withdrawn or pledged until the Court Registry certifies incorporation. The Financial Services Commission may impose an additional minimum net capital requirement when granting the Credit Specialized Financial Business license for factoring.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED: at a duly convened meeting of the initial board of directors of [CORPORATE NAME] (the Company) held on [DATE] at [REGISTERED OFFICE], with the directors present constituting a legal quorum under Article 393 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Articles of Incorporation, the following matters are resolved;

1. Share Capital Subscription. The Board accepts and confirms the subscription list under which the initial paid-up share capital, set at [TOTAL] Korean won, is fully subscribed and allotted, and directs management to require payment of all subscription amounts into the blocked capital-deposit account at [BANK] before filing the incorporation registration. The Board approves issuance of [NUMBER] ordinary shares, with the allocation set out in the shareholder ledger.

2. Banking Authorization. The Board authorizes the opening of operating, escrow, and collection accounts with [BANK] at its [BRANCH] branch and appoints [REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR], [FINANCE DIRECTOR], and [COMPLIANCE OFFICER] as joint authorized signatories, with any disbursement above [THRESHOLD] Korean won requiring two authorized signatures. The banking relationship manager may rely on a certified extract of this resolution for account opening and SWIFT wire operations.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts [ADDRESS] as the registered office of the Company and instructs the representative director to send the required notices to the Court Registry, the district tax office, and the Financial Services Commission or its authorized agent.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR] as Representative Director, [FINANCE DIRECTOR] as Chief Financial Officer, and [COMPLIANCE OFFICER] as Compliance Officer and Anti-Money Laundering Officer. Each officer is vested with all powers granted by the Commercial Act, the Articles of Incorporation, and the Credit Specialized Financial Business Act, subject to board approval thresholds.

5. Secretarial and Filing Direction. The Board directs the Company Secretary to make all incorporation filings, publish any required notices, execute ancillary instruments, and take all steps necessary to give full force and effect to this resolution. The Board further authorizes segregated escrow accounts for receivables collections and reverse factoring settlement, subject to dual-approval controls and Korean GAAP recording.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Reservation and Preparation of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Supreme Court Registration Information System (IROS) and the District Court Registry with jurisdiction over the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an exhaustive availability screening of the proposed Korean corporate name through the IROS front portal and reserve the name electronically. Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation, including a corporate purpose expressed to include accounts receivable factoring, cross-border reverse factoring, trade finance, invoice discounting, and related financing activities, together with the total authorized shares, par value, shares issued at incorporation, subscription price, paid-in amount, registered office address, and promoter arrangements. Identify all promoters, directors, and beneficial owners and perform sanctions screening, source-of-funds review, and conflict-of-interest checks. If a foreign corporate shareholder is involved, collect a certificate of good standing, corporate constitutive documents, and banking reference. Submit the name reservation application and await electronic approval before proceeding to notarization.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Full draft of Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Government-issued photo identification of all promoters and directors
Beneficial ownership declaration and sanctions screening form
Certificate of good standing and constitutional documents of foreign corporate shareholders, apostilled or consular certified
Power of attorney for any local agent or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search returns a conflicting or prohibited name, select an alternative available name and resubmit immediately through the same IROS portal. If the registry issues a request for clarification, respond within the statutory period and correct the Articles of Incorporation or beneficial ownership disclosures before continuing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Inaugural General Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean Notary Public qualified under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange an appointment before a licensed notary public for formal certification of the Articles of Incorporation. All promoters must appear in person or through a validly executed power of attorney, prove identity with a passport or government-issued photo identification, confirm the number of subscribed shares, and acknowledge the articles in their entirety. The notary shall affix the notarial certificate number and seal to the Articles of Incorporation. Following notarization, convene the inaugural general meeting of shareholders to elect the initial directors and the auditor if required by law or internal control rules, and to approve the initial authorized officers and the corporate seal specimen. Record all proceedings in formal minutes signed by the chairperson and attendees. Deliver the notarized articles and minutes to the legal counsel responsible for registration.
required_dossiers: Original Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Government-issued photo identification for each appearing promoter
Notarized power of attorney for each non-appearing promoter
Subscription register and share allocation schedule
Minutes of the inaugural general meeting of shareholders signed by the chairperson
Consent to appointment forms signed by each elected director and auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification due to incomplete identification or ambiguous purpose clauses, revise the Articles of Incorporation to satisfy the notary's statutory objections and reschedule the notarial appointment. If any promoter cannot attend, provide an additional notarized power of attorney and, where required, consular legalization or apostille.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Deposit Account and Payment of Subscription Amounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank or securities company in the Republic of Korea authorized to receive incorporation capital deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital-deposit account in the name of the corporation being formed. Each promoter must transfer the full subscription price into the blocked account using a domestic transfer or SWIFT wire remittance. The account is legally restricted and may not be withdrawn or used for ordinary operations before the Court Registry confirms incorporation. After receipt and verification of funds, the financial institution shall issue a certificate of payment for incorporation, stating the depositor, account number, amount paid, date of payment, and release condition. For non-resident promoters, complete the required foreign exchange declaration or report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and ensure the remittance originates from the promoter's own account. This certificate is mandatory annexure to the registration application. Maintain an audit trail of bank receipts, wire confirmations, and source-of-funds evidence for the anti-money laundering file.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit account opening application
Bank know-your-customer and legal entity identification package
Promoter identification and source-of-funds declarations
Subscription payment instructions and SWIFT wire confirmations
Foreign exchange transaction declaration for any inbound cross-border remittance
Certificate of payment of subscription amount issued by the financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the control structure or ownership, provide an updated corporate diagram, director identification, and the notarized Articles of Incorporation. If the foreign exchange remittance is delayed or blocked, file the required declaration with the responsible foreign exchange bank and resubmit the wire using the corrected remitter information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of Incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registry Division with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, via IROS electronic filing or in-person counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the fully executed application for registration of incorporation with the competent Court Registry. The application must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, the subscription register, minutes of the inaugural general meeting, written consent of the appointed directors and auditor, proof of payment of registration tax and local education tax, and a power of attorney if filed through an agent. The registry will verify the statutory formalities, issue a corporate registration number, and issue a certified certificate of corporate registration. Legal personality commences only upon this registration. After issuance, the representative director must register the corporate seal with the same registry or competent seal registration office and obtain the seal certificate needed for bank accounts and government filings.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation in the official Court Registry form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation in certified true copy form
Certificate of payment of subscription amount from the financial institution
Subscription register and promoter ledger
Minutes of the inaugural general meeting and initial board meeting
Consent to appointment forms for directors and auditor
Registration tax and court fee payment receipt
Power of attorney if filed through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Court Registry issues a notice to correct or supplements, cure the deficiency within the cure period ordinarily allowed, which is five business days, and resubmit the corrected pages with a cover letter referencing the registration number. If the certificate of capital deposit has expired or is defective, obtain a corrected certificate from the financial institution and attach it to the supplemental filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Business Registration and Financial Regulatory License Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district office; Financial Services Commission; Financial Supervisory Service; local fire and safety authorities for ordinary office occupancy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the Court Registry issues the certificate of corporate registration, apply for the business registration certificate for corporate tax purposes at the National Tax Service office having jurisdiction over the registered office. Register the corporate seal and obtain a corporate seal certificate. Open the operating bank account presenting the corporate registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, certified copy of Articles of Incorporation, and the board resolution authorizing signatories. File any required foreign investment or foreign exchange transaction notifications with the responsible bank. For the factoring activity, prepare and submit the Credit Specialized Financial Business license dossier to the Financial Services Commission, including a detailed business plan, financial projections, capital evidence, anti-money laundering program, compliance manual, board resolutions, and organizational chart. This dossier will be scrutinized for regulatory capital, sanctions screening, governance, and consumer protection controls.
required_dossiers: Business registration application for corporate tax
Certificate of corporate registration issued by the Court Registry
Certified copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate card
Board resolution authorizing operating bank account signatories
FSC license application package for factoring and receivables finance
Anti-money laundering policy and beneficial ownership register
Foreign exchange transaction declaration forms for cross-border payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office flags the business address, provide a lease agreement, rent receipt, and building owner consent. If the FSC returns the license application, remedy the identified regulatory capital, governance, or AML deficiencies and refile within 30 days. If the corporate seal registration is refused, correct the director signatures and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission; Financial Supervisory Service; National Tax Service; Ministry of Economy and Finance for foreign exchange transactions; local district office for ordinary commercial occupancy
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Credit Specialized Financial Business License under Article 3 of the Credit Specialized Financial Business Act of the Republic of Korea for factoring, invoice discounting, and accounts receivable financing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; the Ministry of Environment has no jurisdiction over accounts receivable factoring and cross-border reverse factoring because no ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx physical plant, chemical process, assembly operation, or warehouse is being established
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable; no Environmental Impact Assessment, Environmental Registration, or pollution permitting obligation arises from a financial factoring operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; zero process wastewater, zero regulated atmospheric emissions, zero hazardous waste generation, with only ordinary office e-waste managed through municipal collection channels

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to industrial or manufacturing units; the entity must only obtain the standard commercial office fire safety and occupancy approval from the local fire department in the district where the registered office is located, covering fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and electrical safety. No Civil Defense permit is required for a financial factoring and reverse factoring service center.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Korea Customs Service (KCS) UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr) is the integrated customs and export-clearance portal used for export data evidence in the VAT zero-rating regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act and obtain the corporate registration certificate from the court registry office, which generates the corporate registration number. Step 2: Within twenty days from business commencement, file the business registration application with the competent district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered place of business, or through the HomeTax portal, under Article 6 of the Value-Added Tax Act. Step 3: Submit the corporate seal certificate, articles of incorporation, court registration certificate, lease or ownership evidence of the Korean place of business, financial statements or commencement plan, shareholder register, and, for foreign-invested entities, the foreign investment report certificate if applicable under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Step 4: The district tax office issues the ten-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the VAT registration number, corporate tax taxpayer reference, and withholding tax account code. Step 5: A foreign non-resident entity without a Korean establishment that makes taxable supplies in Korea, such as electronic services to Korean consumers, must complete simplified VAT registration through HomeTax and appoint a local tax representative if required; a non-resident enterprise with a permanent establishment follows the same district tax office registration procedure, and the foreign enterprise owner must provide board resolutions, power of attorney, and director identification documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not contain a U.S.-style check-the-box election or a discretionary hybrid-mismatch entity classification regime; a Chusik Hoesa is irrebuttably classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxed on worldwide income at the entity level. A qualifying wholly-owned domestic subsidiary may elect consolidated corporate tax return treatment under the Corporate Tax Act if it satisfies the statutory ownership and filing requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold for a corporation. A Chusik Hoesa is required to register for VAT from the date it commences business activity in Korea, irrespective of annual revenue, because simplified taxpayer status is reserved for individual businesses and is not available to corporations. For reference, an individual whose annual taxable supplies are less than KRW 80,000,000 may qualify as a simplified taxable person, but this status is not available to a Chusik Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Chusik Hoesa, as a corporation, is mandatorily required to issue electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoices) under Article 32 of the Value-Added Tax Act for all taxable supplies to other businesses. e-Tax Invoices are generated through the HomeTax e-Invoice service via the HomeTax web portal, NTS-certified ERP software, or the NTS API, and must be transmitted to the National Tax Service by no later than the day following issuance. The NTS returns a unique acceptance number upon successful transmission, which functions as the anti-fraud digital validation stamp. Correction invoices are separately transmitted, and any mismatched invoice is subject to penalty taxes under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. Korea does not operate a Latin American-style physical fiscal stamp; integrity is achieved through mandatory electronic transmission, acceptance-number tracking, purchaser confirmation on HomeTax, and cross-matching with Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations and foreign exchange bank settlement records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, VAT at 0% applies to exported goods and to specified services supplied to non-residents for use outside Korea. For goods, the statutory evidence is an accepted Korea Customs Service export declaration filed through UNI-PASS showing the Korean supplier as exporter and physical removal of the goods from Korea. For qualifying offshore digital and cross-border services, the supplier must demonstrate that the recipient is established outside Korea, the service is performed or used outside Korea, the contract is with a foreign customer, and payment is received in convertible foreign currency. Material limitation: the factoring fee and discount income of the Chusik Hoesa is a financial service exempt from VAT under Article 26 of the Value-Added Tax Act; therefore the core accounts-receivable factoring and reverse-factoring commissions are not zero-rated and cannot generate an input VAT refund. Zero-rating can be claimed only for any separately taxable goods or services supplied by the Chusik Hoesa, not for the exempt factoring services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS Customs Export Declaration (Export Clearance Certificate) showing the Korean supplier as exporter
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment of goods from Korea
Commercial Invoice and Packing List reconciled with the export declaration
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or foreign currency receipt confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Certificate of Export Performance or other zero-rating export evidence requested by the National Tax Service during audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS operates an integrated VAT control system that automatically cross-matches HomeTax e-Tax Invoices with Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations and foreign exchange settlement records. If zero-rating is claimed without the required customs and foreign-exchange documentation, the supply is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply and assessed at 10% VAT, input VAT attributable to that supply is disallowed, and the related refund is clawed back with penalty surcharges under Articles 47-2 and 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, which can reach up to 40% for fraudulent concealment or unfounded refunds. Criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may follow, exposing responsible parties to imprisonment and fines, and the statute of limitations for collection is extended to ten years in cases of fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized but closely supervised foreign exchange system. Current account transactions are convertible without prior authorization, but all cross-border transfers must be routed through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank and properly documented. Capital account transactions, such as equity injections, shareholder loans, and trade finance cross-border settlements, are generally permitted but trigger mandatory reporting, registration, or approval obligations with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the supervising bank. The Korean won is not a fully internationalized offshore deliverable currency; onshore KRW is freely usable within Korea, but offshore won liquidity and non-deliverable market instruments remain regulated. Export proceeds must be repatriated through a Korean licensed bank within the statutory collection period. Dividend and profit remittances are subject to corporate tax clearance, withholding tax proof, and audited financial statements, but there is no absolute prohibition on profit repatriation. The central bank can impose emergency verification or suspension measures during currency crises, and balance-of-payments and foreign exchange reporting deadlines must be strictly observed. For this factoring entity, convertibility is operationally workable provided that every inbound and outbound remittance is channelled through regulated banks, tagged with the correct Korean FX purpose code, and reconciled with necessary trade documents and tax filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Korean export proceeds must be repatriated into the domestic banking system through a licensed foreign exchange bank within 180 days from the export declaration date, unless an extension of up to six months is pre-approved by the bank due to exceptional trade terms. The full amount of export foreign currency receipts must be collected and credited to a Foreign Exchange Account at a Korean bank or converted into Korean won; there is no partial mandatory surrender ratio, but 100% of export proceeds must ultimately be reported and held inside the authorized Korean banking perimeter.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Standalone fintech EMI viability is legally very low. South Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act restrict foreign exchange business and deposit-taking intermediation to licensed banks and authorized electronic financial companies. A pure offshore fintech EMI cannot open a corporate KRW settlement account or provide escrow and trade factoring clearing without deep sponsorship by a licensed domestic bank. Offshore EMIs such as Wise or Revolut may act as payment transport layers, but they are not acceptable settlement agents for the underlying factoring receivables and cannot satisfy Korean foreign exchange reporting or capital verification requirements. The treasury blueprint should therefore rely on tier-1 commercial banks for all account infrastructure and use fintech products only as ancillary user interfaces connected to a licensed bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks generally require statutory directors or a formally authorized representative with a notarized board resolution and apostilled power of attorney to appear physically in a domestic branch for initial corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a full KYC substitute; it is treated only as auxiliary document authentication. Financial authorities permit non-face-to-face verification in limited low-risk personal banking scenarios, but a corporate Chusik Hoesa engaged in trade finance factoring will be considered medium-to-high risk and will require an in-person principal interview with the compliance team. Non-resident directors should prepare passport copies, visa evidence, overseas proof of address, and a clear explanation of the ultimate ownership chain before the branch visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership through multiple shareholding layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract of the Korean corporate registry and chusik hoesa bylaws, apostilled/consularized articles of incorporation, complete shareholder register showing each natural person, UBO declaration that penetrates all intermediate holding structures, notarized passport copies of each ultimate beneficial owner, and source-of-wealth statements for every material shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing trade factoring license or regulatory authorization
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full banking and financial services compliance file: relevant FSC/MOEF licensing application or regulatory exemption opinion, trade factoring program documents, risk management manual, AML/CFT policy approved by the board, designated compliance officer appointment letter, and a written risk assessment analyzing trade-based financial crime typologies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of fabricated invoices or double factoring of the same receivables
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original export/import sale and purchase contracts, invoice-level reconciliation against customs declarations, validated bills of lading and airway bills, logistics provider confirmations, authenticated receivable assignment register proving no prior assignee claim, external auditor confirmation of receivable ownership, and counterparty corporate KYC files on both the supplier and the obligor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border sanctions exposure in the factoring chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time sanctions screening logs against OFAC, EU, UN, and Korean FSC lists, adverse-media and PEP searches on every entity and signatory, detailed ownership and jurisdiction flowcharts of all underlying trade parties, and qualified legal opinions analyzing trade restrictions and sanctions applicability in each counterparty jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into KR_CHUSIKHOESA must be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 or MT202 transfers from the overseas shareholder's substantive corporate bank account. The transfer must include the correct inward capital FX purpose code as required by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, and the receiving bank will report the transaction to Bank of Korea as part of the balance-of-payments statistics. Funds may be received in USD, EUR, JPY, or CNY and then converted onshore to KRW at the domestic bank's reference rate. The entity must produce the board resolution approving the equity injection, a shareholder investment agreement, source-of-wealth documentation, and the final external audit report confirming paid-in capital; the corporate registry must be amended, and the bank will perform capital verification before funds are available for trade factoring operations. Unlicensed EMIs must not be used for any inbound equity capital because they cannot generate the mandatory BOK reporting proof.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements and factoring proceeds should be cleared exclusively through the domestic tier-1 bank's trade settlement infrastructure. Direct supplier payments and factoring settlements should be made through SWIFT MT103 transfers with the full remittance information and Korean foreign exchange purpose codes. For high-value tends to large import/export contracts, a commercial letter of credit or documentary collection arrangement is appropriate to preserve title and enforce payment conditions. All underlying trade documentation must be retained for at least five years and matched to the bank's foreign exchange reports. Factoring payouts to non-resident parties will trigger foreign exchange reporting, outward remittance tax verification, and reconciliation with the overseas borrowing or assignment agreement; the bank may require evidence of the factorized receivable, assignment notice, and confirmation from the corporate borrower before releasing large cross-border payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts with a licensed domestic bank for documented trade exposure
KRW/CNH and KRW/JPY forward contracts where real export or import flows exist
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) used only for permitted exposure and executed through the domestic bank's non-deliverable forward reporting window
Cross-currency swaps between KRW and settlement currencies for matched factoring assets, subject to real trade exposure documentation and bank/BOK regulatory filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (national corporate tax base) and financial statements attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax, together with local corporate income tax surtax through the competent metropolitan/provincial government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For December 31 fiscal year-end: due by March 31 of the following year, automatically extended to April 30 for companies required to undergo external audit because the audited financial statements are not available earlier; for other fiscal year-ends, due within 3 months of fiscal year-end (Corporate Tax Act).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: additional tax of 20% of unpaid tax (40% if fraudulent non-filing). Underreporting: 10% additional tax (40% if fraudulent). Overdue unpaid tax accrues 0.03% interest per day. Continued non-filing permits seizure of assets, revocation of business registration, and administrative dissolution after persistent dormancy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return (Seoul/local corporate tax levy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (city/province) at registered office address (e.g., Seoul Metropolitan Government through LOCAL-TAX electronic portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as national corporate tax return: within 3 months after fiscal year-end (March 31 for December 31 year-end; April 30 for externally audited corporations) under Local Tax Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: 20% of unpaid local corporate tax as negligent penalty (40% for fraudulent non-filing). Underreporting: 10% (40% if fraudulent). Arrears interest: 0.03% per day. Enforcement includes property attachment and transfer to compulsory tax collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual value-added tax (VAT) return for general taxable corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (January-June): file by July 25 of the same year. Second half (July-December): file by January 25 of the following year. If the deadline falls on a public holiday, the due date shifts to the next business day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled return: additional tax of 10% of the payable VAT (up to 40% for false returns). Underpaid VAT accrues 0.03% per day. Falsified electronic tax invoices carry criminal sanctions and may lead to VAT registration closure and suspension of the factoring/trade-finance license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Year-end wage and salary withholding tax settlement report (including employment income records)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax; Form/IRPM annual wage statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 10 of the following year for the preceding calendar year settlement. For terminating employees, file within the month following the last payment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold or remit employee income taxes: 0.03% per day overdue interest on unremitted amounts; unfiled report penalty of 10% of unpaid tax; criminal liability for embezzlement of withholding taxes; corporate reputation triggers for mandatory tax audit and license review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report and audited financial statements under the Credit Specialized Financial Business Act (trade factoring license)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through FSS e-DICE reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after each business year-end (March 31 for December 31 fiscal year-end); extension may be granted by FSS in exceptional cases.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit: administrative fine up to KRW 30 million (approx. USD 23,000); FSC may issue corrective orders, suspend business activities, impose sanctions on officers, and ultimately revoke the credit-specialized financial business license for chronic non-compliance, which is a functional administrative forfeiture of the factoring license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual external audit report and independent certified CPA audit for licensed financial company or statutory size threshold company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; audited financial statements are also submitted to the shareholders at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external audit must be completed so the audited financial statements can be approved at the annual general meeting, which must be held within 3 months of fiscal year-end (by March 31); for licensed financial companies audited statements are attached to the Annual Business Report due within 90 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Mandated audit omitted: penalty fine up to KRW 30 million and criminal liability for directors under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; FSC may disqualify the external auditor; audit qualification or denial triggers regulatory review and can cause license restriction/revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) supervisory contribution / examination fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) (funded through the Korean Financial Industry Contribution under FSC regulation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: After the FSS issues the annual assessment notice (usually within 60 days after publication of the annual fee schedule and filing of the business report); payment due within 30 days of the assessment notice, or the same deadline as the annual business report if specified in the notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment causes accrual of arrears interest under the State Property Act, collection procedures, suspension of FSS examination clearance, and may be treated as a violation resulting in administrative fine or license revocation for the factoring entity. Because contribution is variable with revenue and assets, no fixed USD amount is set; the fixed government renewal fee element is USD 0.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa engaged in trade/factoring must obtain an independent statutory audit from a licensed certified public accountant if any of the following applies: (1) the company is a licensed credit-specialized financial company under the Credit Specialized Financial Business Act, in which case audit is compulsory regardless of size; (2) total assets at fiscal year-end are at least KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9 million), the general threshold under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; (3) the company is designated by the Financial Services Commission as a public-interest or other specified company because of investor protection, scale of turnover, number of employees, or industry sensitivity; or (4) the company is listed or is a subsidiary included in the consolidation of a public-interest entity. Turnover alone is not a freestanding trigger for ordinary private companies except for FSC designation; however, factoring companies with any asset size are within the mandatory financial-license audit category.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to listed, financial-license and certain public-interest entities; non-financial private companies may apply Korean GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards), but a licensed factoring company must apply K-IFRS or the accounting standards mandated by the FSC and must comply with adequate internal accounting management system rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not operate a one-off or annual public UBO register for ordinary private stock companies. The statutory protocol is comprised of: (a) under Korean Commercial Act, a share transfer is effective against the company only when recorded in the shareholders' register maintained at the head office, and the register must be updated without delay upon any transfer; (b) the licensed factoring company must compile, annually refresh, and make available for FSS inspection a beneficial-ownership KYC file showing ultimate natural person controllers and senior managing officers, consistent with FATF/KoFIU expectations from financial institutions; (c) any acquisition of 10% or more of the issued voting shares of a credit-specialized financial company requires ex-ante approval of the FSC, and any FSC-approved change in major shareholder must be reported to FSS within 30 days; and (d) any other change in shareholding ownership must be recorded in the shareholders' register and reflected in the next annual business report, with no later than 30-day internal compliance update.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Books of Shareholders' General Meetings and Board of Directors' Meetings
Statutory business books and accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 3,500 per year for a registered office address, local corporate secretarial/agent service and registered representative in Seoul or Incheon/Sejong, excluding statutory audit fees and FSS contribution.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000 - USD 75,000 per year for a licensed credit-specialized factoring company, based on a Seoul-area certified CPA firm performing K-IFRS audit plus the required regulatory reporting assistance.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays and preferential deductions under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act include: (1) tax credits for job creation and facility investment; (2) R&D expenditure tax credits; (3) special tax support for SME and venture firms; (4) income deduction for foreign-invested companies under Foreign Investment Promotion Act; (5) increased deductions for personnel working in special economic zones. Factoring companies do not benefit from a general sectoral tax holiday but may apply standard investment and employment credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Beobinse) Form 1 with supporting schedules; filed electronically via HomeTax System (www.hometax.go.kr) operated by the National Tax Service (NTS)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers); one-month automatic extension available upon application; additional extensions for foreign corporations under specific conditions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the domestic business registration number assigned by the Korean tax authority; a foreign corporation without a permanent establishment uses its foreign tax identification number in accordance with NTS guidance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the fiscal period covered by the return; for non-resident corporations, the period must match the Korean taxable year as declared to the NTS.
Report worldwide income if the corporation has a permanent establishment in Korea; only Korean-source income is reportable for non-resident corporations without a permanent establishment.
Claim only deductions permitted under the Corporate Income Tax Act; non-resident corporations without a permanent establishment may only claim expenses directly attributable to Korean-source income.
Compute taxable income after applying deductible expenses, non-taxable income items, and carried-forward losses; non-resident entities must maintain arm's length records.
Apply progressive tax rates: 10% up to KRW 200 million; 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 22% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 25% exceeding KRW 300 billion.
Calculate corporate tax due; non-resident corporations without a permanent establishment are subject to final withholding at the applicable treaty rate.
Report any non-resident tax addition under the Framework Act on National Taxes; penalties apply for failure to report or inaccurate reporting.
Claim eligible foreign tax credits or treaty-based deductions; supporting documentation must be retained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax if filed within 1 month after statutory deadline; 30% if filed between 1 and 3 months late; 40% if filed more than 3 months late. Daily surcharge of 0.022% of unpaid tax per day for overdue amounts. Administrative fine up to KRW 10 million for non-filing under certain conditions. The same sanction framework applies to non-resident corporations having a filing obligation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (resident withholding tax on dividends); non-resident rate is 20% plus local surtax of 2% (total 22%) unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident corporate shareholder must submit to the Korean paying agent a claim form for tax treaty application (Form No. 24 of the Framework Act on National Taxes), accompanied by a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence. The TRC must be apostilled or consularized unless exempt under an Administrative Agreement. The paying agent must file the Form No. 24 with the NTS before making the payment; the reduced withholding rate is applied at source if approval is granted. If the claim is not pre-approved, the excess withheld amount may be reclaimed by filing a corrective return within the statutory period of 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding tax is 20% plus 2% local surtax (aggregate 22%). Treaty rate for royalties is typically 10-15% under the Korea-USA DTA and 10% under the Korea-UK DTA subject to beneficial ownership conditions. Statutory interest withholding tax is 20% plus 2% local surtax (aggregate 22%), reduced to 10-15% under most treaties. For factoring entities, interest-type income from factoring receivables may be classified as interest income; then the reduced treaty rate applies only if the recipient is the beneficial owner. A TRC and Form No. 24 must be submitted for each claim.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory if the related-party transaction amount (per year, per counterparty) exceeds KRW 10 billion (KRW 10,000,000,000); simplified Local File is required when the aggregate related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 5 billion (KRW 5,000,000,000) irrespective of counterparty. A Transaction Summary Report (TSR) is mandatory for transactions exceeding KRW 100 million (KRW 100,000,000) per related party if total related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime akin to offshore financial centres, but a substance-over-form doctrine is embedded in the Corporate Income Tax Act, the Framework Act on National Taxes (anti-abuse rule Article 17-2), and the International Tax Adjustment Act. For a Chusik Hoesa engaged in factoring, the tax authority may recharacterize transactions lacking business purpose, employees, office premises, and real receivable management functions. A factoring entity must demonstrate operational substance through issued factoring contracts, credit evaluation records, collection ledgers, and board resolutions. Shell companies with no Korean economic activity to claim treaty benefits are subject to denial of treaty benefits under the Limitation on Benefits (LOB) provisions of relevant DTAs and under the domestic general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fraudulent omission of factoring income, fabrication of bad debt allowances, unlawful claim of non-deductible reserves, or underreporting of interest/commission income from factoring transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 3 times the evaded tax amount under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; additionally, the NTS imposes 40% negligence penalty and 20% underreporting penalty on the evaded tax plus 0.022% daily surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally or negligently participate in tax evasion may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax arrears under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 39. Criminal imprisonment applies to acting directors; travel bans are automatically issued for tax arrears above KRW 50 million. Civil restitution may extend to unjust enrichment received by directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Chusik Hoesa that records factoring transactions but has no physical office, employees, decision-making functions, or actual cash flows; using the entity as a conduit for treaty shopping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, imposition of 20% penalty on the taxable amount adjusted, and refusal of foreign tax credit. Under the International Tax Adjustment Act, a 20% penalty may be imposed on the amount of income derived from a transaction lacking economic substance; the entity may additionally lose its corporate identity for tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve artificial interposed structures may be personally assessed for the corporate tax under the actual management liability principle; the NTS may pierce the veil where the entity is used as a fraud instrument. Travel bans and asset seizures are available for outstanding corporate liabilities exceeding KRW 50 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Factoring operations conducted without a statutory license under the Factoring Act or utilizing unregistered escrow accounts; acceptance of illicit funds or failure to report suspicious transactions under the Financial Transactions Reports Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to KRW 10 million for conducting unlicensed financial business; the Financial Services Commission may revoke registration and impose administrative fines up to KRW 100 million. For violation of reporting duties, imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to KRW 20 million for individual violations; additional fines for the corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for breach of fiduciary duty to maintain AML compliance; they may be jointly and severally liable for restitution of fraudulently transferred funds. Travel bans are imposed in case of criminal prosecution; imprisonment sentences are served individually.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain required Local/Master File and Transaction Summary Report (TSR); manipulating the arm's length interest rate on factoring advances to shift profits to a related party in a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS adjustment of the taxable income under the arm's length principle; 20% penalty on the adjusted amount and an additional 10% penalty for failure to submit TP documentation; daily surcharge applies from the date the return was due. If foreign tax credit claimed without proper documentation, the credit is denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign a false transfer pricing filing or who are involved in the preparation of flawed documentation may be personally fined up to KRW 10 million under the Framework Act on National Taxes; civil liability for the unpaid tax difference may be imposed in case of willful neglect.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a foreign parent without withholding the applicable 22% statutory tax or without verifying treaty eligibility through TRC and Form No. 24.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is personally liable for the unwithheld amount plus an additional 10% negligence penalty, and the recipient remains liable for unpaid tax; daily surcharge applies. In serious cases, criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may be initiated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly effect a foreign payment without withholding are jointly liable for the unremitted tax and may be subjected to travel bans and asset freezes; criminal imprisonment up to 2 years may be imposed for intentional violation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing false tax invoices for factoring service fees, omission of VAT-exempt supply or non-taxable income in the VAT return, or claiming input VAT on non-business expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT penalty of 2% of the falsely issued invoice amount; omitted VAT subject to 40% penalty plus daily surcharge; issuance of false VAT invoice carries criminal imprisonment up to 2 years and fine up to 2 times the VAT evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who oversee invoicing and VAT returns are personally liable for unpaid VAT if they are found to be the actual business operator; for criminal violation, imprisonment is served personally.
